events.title: Ask Us Anything (We Might Know) with Paul Barrett & Jamie Kriegel
events.description:
You can find plenty of places to learn the mechanics of Agile. This gathering is about the moments that happen after the mechanics.

The conversation that doesn't go the way you expected. The team whose energy slowly disappeared. The Product Owner whose priorities seem to shift every week. The stakeholder searching for certainty while the ground keeps moving. The retrospective that left everyone feeling farther apart than when it started. That one "nobody wants to talk about it" question that lingers in your mind. Bring the questions you've been carrying around. The stories you've been meaning to tell. The situations that made you wonder whether anyone else has ever sat where you're sitting.

We'll explore them together.

Some conversations will uncover an answer. Others will reveal a better question. Every so often, someone across the room will describe an experience that suddenly gives language to something you've been feeling for months.

This is simply a room full of thoughtful people who care about teams, leadership, and learning. People willing to share what worked, what didn't, and what they discovered along the way. Whether you're discovering Scrum for the first time, coaching seasoned organizations, or leading people through the uncertainty that seems to find all of us eventually, there's a place for you here.

Bring your curiosity.

Go home a little wiser than you arrived.

events.title: AI in QA Automation: Where It Helps, Where It Doesn't (Yet)
events.description: AI is showing up everywhere in software delivery - including testing - but most teams are still figuring out where it actually moves the needle versus where it's just noise. In this session, Saurabh Sharma will walk through the current landscape of AI in QA automation: what's genuinely reducing manual testing overhead and flaky test maintenance, what's still overhyped, and the real challenges organizations run into when they try to bring AI into their QA and CI/CD workflows (including the newer problem of testing AI agents themselves for accuracy and reliability). Expect a practical, pain-points-first conversation - with plenty of room for questions from teams navigating this shift in their own sprints.

events.title: Agile Coaching in the Age of AI with Bob Galen
events.description:
There is an incredible amount of discussion around the role of AI in your Agile Coaching. How can you weave it into the coaching conversations, guidance, metrics, and client outcomes?

It’s an incredibly exciting time, and those who ignore the implications, quite frankly, will have missed the boat.

But . . .

That’s not what we’ll be talking about in this session. Here we’re going to explore HI (Human Intelligence) and the tension AI plays in developing and accelerating your HI.

We’ll explore what it looks like from the perspective of Agile Coaching skills and competencies.

For example:

* The core skill mix that will differentiate you from other coaches and their AI.
* What are the keys to being effective in organizational and AI transformations?
* How to effectively communicate, including your value proposition aligned with AI.
* Finally, how to avoid jumping on the AI bandwagon and losing your HI edge.

In a word, this session is all about YOU.

How to develop your HI competitive edges so that you can partner with AI and not lose yourself and your unique value in the process.

Disclaimer: This is not an AI talk ![😉](https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/e/notoemoji/17.0/1f609/32.png)

events.title: AI as Your Second Brain
events.description:
***Cross-posting! We are joining with AgileBoston for this one! Please note, Zoom link not included. Please go [here](https://us06web.zoom.us/meeting/register/tJMqcu2qqz8iEt0zlAlKvvtnCxZrRug3-UB1#/registration) to register in advance.***

*How I use AI to remember what my human brain can't, and show up as a better practitioner.*

Most of us have tried an AI chat and received a decent answer. Far fewer have built it into how we work. I'll show what that looks like in practice: a personal knowledge system that turns meeting transcripts into decisions and action items, remembers what each stakeholder cares about, and preps me for the next conversation before I walk in.

What surprised me was how human it makes the work. When I ask for a prep brief and get reminded that a teammate raised a concern three weeks ago, I show up as someone who listened. We'll walk through the system live, look at where it has earned my trust and where it needs a skeptical read, and talk about what Scrum Masters, Product Owners, and coaches might want their own second brain to remember.

**You'll leave with**

* A repeatable workflow from meeting to synthesis to next-meeting prep that you can try this week.
* A simple rule for deciding when to trust AI output, when to treat it as a draft, and when to expect it to be wrong.
* Ideas for what context is worth capturing about your teams and stakeholders, and what isn't.

**Audience:** Scrum Masters, Product Owners, Agile coaches, and anyone who spends the day in back-to-back conversations. No technical background needed.

**Format:** Conversational, with a live demo and discussion pauses.

events.title: The Agile Credibility Crisis: Reclaiming the Scrum Master with AI Agents
events.description:
Many enterprise leaders see the Scrum Master as a tactical necessity, not a strategic asset. As AI starts handling ticket triage and calendar management, our credibility depends on the coaching work only we can do.

In this session we'll map the "administrative drift" that turns Scrum Masters into clerks. Then I'll show how proactive AI agents can take over status reporting and event scheduling, giving back 10+ hours a week for flow, stakeholder alignment and real improvement work.

We'll start with a quick diagnostic where you plot your own week: admin work vs. strategic coaching. We'll finish with a Capacity Reclamation Audit. You'll leave with one task to automate and one new signal to track starting Monday.

events.title: Clarity Governs the System: Rethinking Planning & Problem Solving in Agile
events.description:
There is no shortage of frameworks, methodologies, tools, and practices designed to help organizations improve how they work, solve problems, and deliver value.

Yet, despite all these approaches, organizations continue to struggle with challenges that seem to persist regardless of how much effort is invested in solving them.

Why?

Could it be that we're sometimes attempting to solve problems we haven't fully understood?

Or that we're solving individual problems without recognizing how they are interconnected?

And perhaps more importantly, how do we know we're solving the problems that will actually move us closer to our overarching goals?

In this session, we'll explore a foundational principle of The SP&PS™ (Strategic Planning & Problem Solving) System:

**Clarity Governs the System.**

Together, we'll challenge some familiar assumptions and explore:

* Why identifying a problem isn't necessarily the same as understanding it.
* The relationship between strategic planning, interrelated problems, and overarching goals.
* Why clarity must govern more than just the beginning of an initiative.
* What these principles mean for Scrum Masters, Agile Coaches, Product Managers, and transformation leaders.

We'll also introduce The SP&PS™ System, a system developed to approach strategic planning and problem solving as interconnected disciplines.

This isn't another Agile framework or a discussion about adopting the latest methodology.

**It's an opportunity to rethink how we navigate from what is to what should be.**

Come prepared to question assumptions, share experiences, and engage in a conversation that may challenge how you think about strategic planning and problem solving
